buzz.title: Daily Buzz
buzz.content:
━━ LOCAL ━━

1) CRYSTAL MOUNTAIN COULD SELL OR TAKE ON A PARTNER
• Family is exploring a sale OR a partner, and MacInnes says "we don't have to really sell"
• Benzie County's largest employer, running business as usual
• $200 million+ invested since 1989, 70 years old this year
• Any buyer needs deep pockets AND matching values
➜ TAKE: Crystal is where half of Northern Michigan learned to ski and the other half learned to fall down. Whoever buys it better keep the Buck in Buck Hills.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: what's your best Crystal Mountain memory?

2) SANDHILL CRANES ARE PEAKING RIGHT NOW
• Migration peaks right about now, mid-November
• Hundreds to thousands roost in shallow wetlands and feed in harvested corn fields
• That bugling, "prehistoric" call is what you're hearing overhead
• Mild weather could keep them in Michigan into December
➜ TAKE: If you heard a pterodactyl over the Meijer parking lot this weekend, relax. It was a sandhill crane.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: where have you seen the biggest flock of cranes up here?

3) FISHPASS IS GETTING A KAYAK SLIDE
• New aluminum kayak slide and launch at the Union Street Dam
• Paddle from Boardman Lake to Grand Traverse Bay without hauling your boat
• Still under construction, opening expected summer 2027
➜ TAKE: A water slide for grown-ups in the middle of downtown. I've never wanted summer 2027 more.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: would you be first in line to ride the kayak slide, or is that a hard no?

━━ BITS ━━

50s IN NOVEMBER
• It's mid-November and we're near 60 all week. Are you putting the Christmas lights up NOW in the sunshine, or waiting until it's 20 and sleeting like a true Michigander?

THE THERMOSTAT WAR
• It's that time of year. What's the number in your house, 68 or 70, and who keeps sneaking over to change it?

THE GERMAN FOOTBALL KING
• The Lions played in Munich in front of a record crowd. If the Lions played overseas again, would you go? And what city?

━━ SPORTS ━━

KINGSLEY IS GOING TO THE SEMIS (12-0)
• Kingsley 34, Sanford Meridian 28, Division 6 regional final Friday at Kingsley, in the snow
• Down 22-14 at halftime, the Stags scored in the final minute, then a sack with 13 seconds left sealed it
• NEXT: Division 6 state semifinal vs. Almont (12-0), Saturday, Nov. 21, at Clare High School (time TBA)
• Going for a second straight trip to the state final

ST. FRANCIS VOLLEYBALL'S RUN ENDS
• Calumet beat St. Francis 3-0 (25-19, 25-8, 25-10) in Thursday's Division 3 regional final in Manistique
• The Gladiators finish 30-18-2

BAY REPS HOCKEY IS UNBEATEN
• Boys: beat Alpena 3-1 Saturday and Cranbrook 4-2 Thursday, now 2-0
• Girls: 3-0 to start, outscoring teams 22-2 over the weekend

UP NORTH STATE RUNS
• Gaylord St. Mary (12-0) beat Portland St. Patrick 39-36 and plays for the 8-player Division 2 title vs. Mendon (12-0), Saturday, Nov. 21, 2 PM at the Superior Dome in Marquette, its first final since 2002
• Roscommon volleyball plays Calumet in a Division 3 state quarterfinal Tuesday, 6 PM, in Gaylord
• Charlevoix's football season ended at Menominee Saturday
• Every other area team on our list is done for the season

LIONS 35, PATRIOTS 10 (7-2)
• Five straight wins, in Munich, in front of a record crowd of 70,225
• Amon-Ra St. Brown ran out with a German flag and scored twice, including a 56-yarder
• Jahmyr Gibbs: 252 total yards and two TDs
• Bad news: Aidan Hutchinson hurt his right knee celebrating a sack, and an AP source says it's season-ending

MICHIGAN AND MICHIGAN STATE
• Michigan lost at No. 18 Oregon, 31-7
• Michigan State lost to Washington, 21-14

mental.title: Mental Health Minute
mental.content:
Park the List Before Bed

We've got a sunny, mild week ahead, which is great, but Thanksgiving is now ten days out, and if your brain is anything like mine, it's already running the grocery list and the guest list at two in the morning. That happens because when we leave things undone, our mind keeps them on a loop so we don't forget them, and the loop doesn't care that you're trying to sleep. So here's your move for today. Tonight, before you turn out the light, grab a piece of paper and write down tomorrow's to-do list, the pie, the phone call, the thing you keep forgetting at the store. Researchers at Baylor University found that people who wrote out tomorrow's to-do list before bed fell asleep faster than people who didn't, because once it's on paper, your brain can finally let go of it. So put the list on the nightstand and let it hold the worry for you until morning. That's your Mental Health Minute on Z93. Text me at 231-929-4487 and tell me the one thing that's at the top of your list.
mental.notes:
Evidence: Scullin et al., 2018, Journal of Experimental Psychology: General (Baylor University). Writing a specific to-do list before bed was linked to falling asleep faster than writing about completed tasks. This is a sleep-onset finding, not a clinical claim.
Move is new this week (week-used reset). It's different from last week's 'Let the Phone Sleep in the Kitchen.' Indoor move, fine for any weather.

"BABY, SHE'S BACK!" SPACEX CATCHES STARSHIP · BUFFER: NEWSY VIRAL
• SpaceX's launch tower caught a returning Starship for the first time, and the crowd lost it
🔊 IN: "There's the sonic boom. Starship returning." (4:46) → "Let's go Ship 42" (4:57)
then: "Mechazilla has caught the Starship..." (6:43) OUT: "...Baby, she's back." (6:55)
~25 s edited · PLAY
➜ WHY: A real 'you had to hear it' moment, a sonic boom plus a screaming crowd, and it works without the picture

events.notes:
Buck Pole: 9&10 News 11/15, UpNorthLive. Light Up/Parade: UpNorthLive (last week) and the downtowntc.com events page. Semis/finals: Oakland Press pairings 11/14.
Town buzz (not carded): Boardman River wall emergency repairs could start within weeks, a $252,000 job the city commission still has to confirm next week (Record-Eagle via Daily Traverse City 11/15). That's the third week of river-wall news, so give it a self-aware nod if it's used.
